A transgender military member has been fined in a case where she was Tasered while fighting to have her gender identity changed on her file.

Royal Canadian Air Force Sgt. Athena Morris was fined $2,000 for unlawfully entering a restricted area at 17 Wing Winnipeg on March 31, 2025, when she demanded the gender marker on her file be changed. Morris, a transgender woman, said she had been trying to get her gender identifier changed since January of that year.

The incident was a culmination of “months of friction,” defence counsel Maj. Carlos Da Cruz told military judge Stephen Strickey Monday during a hearing at HMCS Chippawa, a Royal Canadian Navy Reserve division in Winnipeg.

JOHN WOODS / FREE PRESS FILES

The main gate at Canadian Forces Base 17 Wing in Winnipeg.

Da Cruz told court Morris was misgendered by colleagues and superiors and told she wasn’t allowed to use the women’s bathrooms or showers.

“Despite this, she tried to do things the right way,” Da Cruz said. “Instead of being assisted, she was incorrectly turned away by staff.”

On the day of the incident, Morris went to an administrative counter at the military base to ask that her gender identification be changed. Staff refused the request because they believed she didn’t have the right documents to make the change.

In protest, she went over the counter, entered an orderly’s office and tied herself to a chair with a scarf and refused to leave until the change was made. Military police were called and, when she resisted arrest, she was shocked with a Taser and forcibly removed.

She was jolted a second time while handcuffed in the military police cruiser, which Strickey ruled was an excessive use of force in a decision last week.
